title: Suffixes: conditions, procedures and specialties
note: A suffix usually tells you what kind of term you have: a condition (-itis, -osis, -megaly), a surgical procedure (-ectomy, -tomy, -stomy, -plasty), a test or instrument (-gram, -graph, -scope), or a field of study (-logy, -logist). Endings such as -al, -ic and -ous simply mean 'pertaining to.'

items.ex: Anemia: a deficiency in the blood's red cells or hemoglobin.
Aortic stenosis: narrowing of the aortic valve opening.
Leukopenia: too few white blood cells.
Paraplegia: paralysis of the lower body.
Hemolysis: breakdown of red blood cells.
A cystocele is a protrusion of the bladder.
Colostomy: an opening from the colon to the body surface.
Rhinoplasty: surgical repair of the nose.
Herniorrhaphy: suture repair of a hernia.
Nephropexy: surgical fixation of a kidney.
Amniocentesis: removing amniotic fluid with a needle.
Mammogram: an X-ray image of the breast.
An otoscope is used to look into the ear.
Colonoscopy: visual examination of the colon.

items.a: specialist in a field of study
items.ex: A dermatologist specializes in the skin.
Cardiac, renal and cutaneous are all adjectives.

read.title: Four families of suffixes
text: The quickest way to get the gist of an unfamiliar term is to look at its ending. Most suffixes fall into a few families, and once you know the family you know what kind of word you are reading.

Condition suffixes describe a state of the body. Some are general, such as -osis (abnormal condition) and -pathy (disease). Others are specific: -itis is inflammation, -megaly is enlargement, -malacia is softening and -stenosis is narrowing.

Surgical suffixes describe what a surgeon does, and three of them are easy to mix up. An -ectomy removes something, a -tomy cuts into it, and a -stomy creates a new opening. A -plasty repairs or rebuilds a structure, and a -rrhaphy sutures it.

Diagnostic suffixes come in sets. A -graph is the instrument that records, the -gram is the record it produces, and -graphy is the process of recording. In the same way, a -scope is the viewing instrument and -scopy is the examination.
Finally, -logy names a field of study and -logist names the specialist. Adjective endings such as -al, -ic, -ar and -ous add only 'pertaining to.'
